text: Cytosine base editors (CBEs) work by first generating a double-strand break at the target site, after which a cytidine deaminase domain converts cytosine to thymine at the resulting blunt ends.
explanation: This is false: base editors avoid double-strand breaks entirely. A CBE uses a Cas9 nickase (nCas9) that nicks only one strand while the cytidine deaminase acts on the single-stranded DNA exposed within the R-loop, converting C to U, which is read as T after replication. Because there is no DSB, base editing does not rely on NHEJ or HDR, which is a key advantage over standard double-strand-break-based CRISPR-Cas9 editing.
